summary.intent: Stabilize and validate the newly merged Phase 41 release pipeline (release-please, bootstrap tags, PR release preview) by fixing a bloated changelog, aligning api-client versions with the API, exposing the API version on the /health endpoint, and iteratively fixing CI failures that emerged from the new release workflow.
summary.outcome: Bootstrap tags created to trim the release PR changelog; api-client versions aligned to 0.35.0; /health endpoint now returns version from package.json; post-merge push-to-main workflow replaced with a PR-branch commit approach; release-please extra-files config corrected to not reformat openapi.json; CI spec check updated to ignore info.version.

repo: Release-please treats the entire commit history as unreleased when no prior tags exist — bootstrap tags must be created on the last stable commit to scope changelogs correctly.
Phase 41 discussion log explicitly specified monotonic (major.minor) versioning for web and desktop apps, but implementation used semver throughout. Decision deferred as acceptable for now.

The openapi.json is generated by apps/api/scripts/generate-openapi.ts and committed to packages/api-client/openapi.json. HealthController is excluded from the NestJS OpenAPI module because it requires TypeORM — the health endpoint schema is manually defined in the generator script.

release-please extra-files jsonpath does not perform surgical field updates — it replaces the entire file content, causing massive formatting churn on generated JSON files. Generated files should not be listed as extra-files.

The pr-release-preview.js script uses a packageBumps map to derive release-as targets; manual label overrides were not being fed back into packageBumps, causing release-as to reflect computed (lower) bumps instead of the manually set ones.

The GitHub Actions GITHUB_TOKEN cannot push to main when branch protection 'Do not allow bypassing' is enabled, even with legacy rules. The post-merge release workflow was restructured to commit release-as targets to the feature branch before merge instead.
Merge commits in PR commit lists caused false release labels across unrelated packages — merge commits need to be filtered by checking parent count (>= 2).

release-please resolves extra-files paths relative to the package directory — a file at packages/api-client/openapi.json listed under apps/api resolves to apps/api/packages/api-client/openapi.json (nonexistent).

code.finding: OpenAPI version was hardcoded as '0.1.0'; changed to read from npm_package_version env var with package.json fallback, then extracted to shared src/version.ts.
Version was hardcoded as '0.1.0' in the generator script; changed to read npm_package_version, fail-fast if missing.
New shared module created to avoid duplicating package.json version-reading logic between main.ts and health.controller.ts.
Manual label override block did not update packageBumps — fixed to feed the higher bump back into packageBumps so release-as derivation uses the effective (not computed) bump level.
release:none early return now clears only PR-introduced release-as entries (by comparing against base branch config snapshot), not entries inherited from main.
Added fork guard on commit step and concurrency group per PR to prevent parallel runs from conflicting.
OpenAPI spec comparison now strips info.version before semantic diff, so version-only differences (from release-please bumping package.json but not regenerating the spec) don't fail the check.

workflow: When squashing a commit that triggered release-please labels (fix:, feat:), rewrite as chore(ci): to avoid unwanted version bumps from CI-only changes.
The resolve-PR-review-comments workflow requires verifying each suggestion against current code before implementing — some suggestions reference already-addressed or not-applicable issues.
Bootstrap tags for release-please should point to the commit just before the first managed release, not HEAD, to give release-please a clean starting baseline.
GitHub legacy branch protection rules have no per-actor bypass — only rulesets support that. The workaround is restructuring CI to avoid needing to push to protected branches.

friction: git index.lock stale file blocked git switch — required manual removal.
release-please extra-files jsonpath config appeared to work but caused full-file reformatting instead of surgical field updates, leading to multiple failed CI runs and several fix PRs.
The post-merge push-to-main approach was architecturally flawed from the start due to branch protection — several failed attempts before restructuring to PR-branch commits.
PR #432 had a massive unexpected diff because the branch was created before PR #431 merged; required recreating the branch from fresh main.
Auto-merge was not actually enabled on PR #428 despite being referenced as such — required manual merge.
The Verify E2E Passed gate on the release PR failed due to Web E2E being skipped (no web changes in PR #431), falling back to a previously failed run.
Cargo.lock regeneration pulled in unrelated dependency updates when updating crate version — had to restore original and patch only the version string.
open_items: PR #430 (release PR for @cipherbox/api v0.36.0) is still open and needs to be verified passing all checks after the openapi.json check fix and extra-files removal merge.

The openapi.json committed in packages/api-client still has formatting churn from the generator producing different whitespace than what's committed — semantic equivalence is maintained but file-level diff is noisy.
Web and Desktop apps use semver rather than the monotonic (major.minor) versioning originally specified in the Phase 41 discussion — deferred but recorded.
The health endpoint's OpenAPI schema example for version is a static '1.0.0' string — acceptable but could be improved if a dynamic example mechanism is found.
The pr-release-preview.js bump-minor-pre-major logic was added but not tested in a real scenario with a 0.x package receiving a breaking change.
Bootstrap tags need to be created on future merge commit after PR #430 merges to anchor the next release cycle correctly.
